name: Initial unemployment insurance claim at a US state agency
summary: A worker who has lost a job files an initial claim for unemployment insurance with the state agency, which must confirm identity, check that past wages are high enough, learn from the employer why the job ended, and decide any eligibility question before paying benefits. Most claims are paid automatically about two to three weeks after filing, once the waiting week and first payable week have passed. About a third need an adjudicator to interview the claimant and employer about a quit or discharge, and denied claimants can appeal to a hearing officer. Elapsed time is driven by the weekly certification calendar, adjudication queues and appeal hearing schedules, all of which lengthened sharply in the 2020 to 2022 claim surge.

baseline.org_archetype: A mid-size US state workforce agency handling about 12,000 new initial claims a month in normal conditions, with an online claim system, a contact center, an adjudication unit and an appeals tribunal.
baseline.notes: Timings are calibrated to 2019 national ETA data (normal operations); 2020 to 2022 benchmarks show the surge and backlog conditions of the same period. Pandemic programs (PUA, PEUC) are out of scope.

unit_of_work: one new initial claim for regular state unemployment insurance
trigger: The claimant files an initial claim online or by phone after losing work.
end_state: The first payment is issued, the claim is denied or abandoned with no appeal, or a first-level or higher-authority appeal decision is issued.

volume.seasonality: Peaks in January and early July (seasonal layoffs) and in recessions; in April and May 2020 claims ran at many times normal levels.

evidence.note: National new intrastate claims were 7.24 million in 2019 (about 600,000 a month); a mid-size state with about 2% of the national workload files about 12,000 a month. 2020 national claims were 7.6 times 2019.

triggered_by.from: Employer mass layoff or attached claim filing

produces.object: first benefit payment and continued weekly claims
benefit charges to the employer account
claimant referral for work search and reemployment assessment

systems.name: State UI benefits system (mainframe or modernized) with online claim filing
Identity and integrity cross-matches (Social Security number verification, national integrity data hub, new hire, prison)
Employer separation information exchange or mailed request form
Appeals case management and hearing scheduling system
Payment file to bank for direct deposit or debit card

steps.name: Claimant files initial claim
steps.description: The claimant files online or by phone, giving identity details, employers in the last 18 months, the reason for separation, and answers to eligibility questions about availability for work, other income and pensions, and registers for work as state law requires.

error.defect_description: Wrong employer, wrong separation reason or missing out-of-state wages.

evidence.note: 7.24 million new intrastate claims were filed in 2019. Claimant time is outside the agency and is not counted as hands-on time.

steps.name: Run identity and integrity cross-matches
steps.description: The benefits system verifies the Social Security number and runs overnight cross-matches against integrity databases, new hire and prison records and earlier claims, and flags claims whose identity cannot be confirmed automatically.

error.defect_description: A false identity passes the automated checks.

control.basis: State UI law and US Department of Labor integrity requirements to verify claimant identity and Social Security number before payment

evidence.note: Standard practice; the 10% flag rate is an estimate for normal years and was several times higher in 2020 and 2021 during the fraud wave.

steps.name: Claimant completes identity verification
steps.description: The flagged claimant receives a notice asking for proof of identity and uploads a photo identification and proof of address, completes online identity proofing, or visits an office.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Estimate based on common practice.

steps.name: Contact center helps claimant with identity issue
steps.description: A contact center agent answers or returns the claimant's call, looks up the claim, explains which documents are needed and how to upload them, and notes the call on the claim record.

error.defect_description: Wrong instructions given, so the claimant uploads the wrong document.

evidence.note: Hold times and callbacks vary greatly; in 2020 contact centers were overwhelmed. Estimate for normal operations.

steps.name: Review identity documents
steps.description: A claims examiner opens the uploaded documents, compares name, date of birth, Social Security number and address with the claim and wage records, and clears the identity hold or denies the claim for failure to verify identity.

error.defect_description: A forged document is accepted.

control.basis: State UI law and US Department of Labor integrity requirements on identity verification

evidence.note: Estimate based on common practice.

steps.name: Issue monetary determination
steps.description: The system pulls the claimant's base-period wages from the quarterly wage records, applies the state's earnings tests, computes the weekly benefit amount and maximum duration, and mails or posts the monetary determination.

error.defect_description: Wages missing from the base period, for example an employer that reported late or out-of-state work.

control.basis: State UI law base-period wage and earnings requirements (monetary eligibility)

next.condition: insufficient wages; claimant does not dispute

evidence.note: 10.1% of 2019 monetary determinations found insufficient wage credits; the split between disputes and accepted ineligibility is an estimate.

steps.name: Investigate wages and redetermine
steps.description: A claims examiner reviews the claimant's pay stubs or W-2s, contacts the employer or another state for missing wages, adds the wages to the record and issues a redetermination.

error.defect_description: Wages added to the wrong quarter, changing the benefit amount.

control.basis: State UI law on monetary redetermination and wage investigation

evidence.note: Estimate based on common practice.

steps.name: Send separation information request to the employer
steps.description: The system sends the last employer a request for the reason for separation through the electronic exchange or by mail, with a deadline of about 10 days, and charges notice for experience rating.

error.defect_description: Request sent to a wrong or old employer address.

control.basis: State UI law notice to the last employer and opportunity to provide separation information (Social Security Act s. 303(a)(1) methods of administration)

evidence.note: Standard practice; deadline is set by each state.

steps.name: Claimant certifies the waiting week and first compensable week
steps.description: After each week ends the claimant files a weekly certification online or by phone, reporting earnings, availability, work search and any job refusals; in most states the first week is an unpaid waiting week.

error.defect_description: Earnings or availability misreported.

control.basis: State UI law weekly eligibility conditions: able, available and actively seeking work

evidence.note: 20 CFR 640.5 measures timeliness from the end of the first compensable week, which in waiting-week states ends about two weeks after filing. Wait is the calendar time to that point.

steps.name: Employer returns separation information
steps.description: The employer's payroll or third-party claims administrator returns the separation reason, often contesting a quit or discharge, or does not respond by the deadline.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Mostly arrives during the certification wait, so only the late tail is added; estimate.

steps.name: Screen claim for eligibility issues
steps.description: The system compares the claimant's separation reason, certification answers and the employer's response, sets an issue for any quit, discharge, availability, refusal or income question, and otherwise releases the claim for payment.

error.defect_description: A disqualifying issue is not detected and is found later by audit or cross-match.

next.condition: nonseparation issue blocks the first payment

evidence.note: 2019: 0.26 separation determinations per initial claim (new and additional) and 0.40 per new claim; 0.33 is used. The nonseparation share before first payment is an estimate.

steps.name: Assign adjudicator and schedule fact-finding
steps.description: The adjudication unit assigns the issue to an adjudicator, who reviews the claim, the employer's statement and prior claims, and sends both parties a notice of a scheduled phone fact-finding interview.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Queue wait set so detection-to-determination matches the 2019 median band of 15 to 21 days in ETA 9052.

steps.name: Conduct fact-finding interviews
steps.description: The adjudicator calls the claimant and the employer, asks about the events leading to the separation, records each statement and any documents such as warnings or resignation letters, and offers rebuttal; employers often do not answer.

error.defect_description: Key facts not obtained because a party could not be reached.

evidence.note: Estimate based on common practice.

steps.name: Decide and write the separation determination
steps.description: The adjudicator weighs the statements against the state's voluntary quit and misconduct provisions, writes a determination with findings of fact, reasoning and appeal rights, and issues it to the claimant and employer.

error.defect_description: Determination below the federal quality standard, for example missing facts or wrong legal reasoning.

control.basis: State UI law disqualification provisions; Social Security Act s. 303(a)(1) methods of administration; DOL nonmonetary determination timeliness (80% within 21 days) and quality standards

evidence.note: 47.7% of 2019 separation determinations were denials. The 35% appeal rate after a denial is an estimate consistent with 0.133 appeals per new claim nationally.

steps.name: Adjudicate a nonseparation issue
steps.description: The adjudicator contacts the claimant about availability, a job refusal, school attendance or other income, reviews documents, and issues a determination allowing or denying the affected weeks.

error.defect_description: Determination below the federal quality standard.

control.basis: State UI law able and available and suitable work provisions; DOL nonmonetary timeliness and quality standards

evidence.note: 2019: 83.8% of nonseparation determinations within 21 days of detection. Shares are estimates for issues that block the first payment.

steps.name: Release the first payment
steps.description: With the weeks certified and no pending issue, the nightly payment run calculates the payment for the first compensable week, applies tax withholding if chosen, and sends it by direct deposit or debit card.

error.defect_description: Payment amount wrong because of misreported earnings.

control.basis: Social Security Act s. 303(a)(1) full payment when due; 20 CFR 640.5 first payment promptness (87% within 14 or 21 days)

next.condition: employer appeals an allowed separation determination

evidence.note: 2019: 55.4% of first payments within 7 days and 82.4% within 14 days of the end of the first compensable week. The employer appeal share is derived from ETA 5130 (about 20% of appeals are by employers).

steps.name: Claimant files an appeal
steps.description: The denied claimant files an appeal online, by mail or by fax within the state's deadline, usually 10 to 30 days, often continuing to certify weeks while the appeal is pending.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Appeal deadlines vary by state; timing is an estimate.

steps.name: Docket the appeal and schedule a hearing
steps.description: The appeals clerk creates the appeal case, attaches the determination and claim file, schedules a telephone hearing with a hearing officer, and mails notices to both parties at least several days in advance.

error.defect_description: Notice sent to an old address, causing a missed hearing.

evidence.note: Estimate based on common practice.

steps.name: Conduct the appeal hearing
steps.description: The hearing officer reviews the file, holds a recorded telephone hearing with the claimant, the employer and witnesses, takes testimony and exhibits under oath, and closes the record.

error.defect_description: Procedural defect such as failure to develop the record.

control.basis: Social Security Act s. 303(a)(3) opportunity for a fair hearing; 20 CFR 650.4 appeals promptness (60% within 30 days, 80% within 45)

evidence.note: 2019: 72.0% of first-level decisions within 30 days and 90.2% within 45 days of the appeal; waits are set to match.

steps.name: Write and issue the appeal decision
steps.description: The hearing officer writes the decision with findings of fact and conclusions of law, affirming or reversing the determination, and mails it with rights to a further appeal.

error.defect_description: Decision reversed on further appeal for legal error.

next.condition: decided in favor of the claimant; benefits payable
further appeal to the board of review

evidence.note: 32.3% of 2019 lower authority decisions favored the appellant. The further-appeal share is an estimate.

steps.name: Board of review decides higher-authority appeal
steps.description: The board of review or higher-authority referee reviews the hearing record and written arguments, usually without a new hearing, and issues a decision affirming, reversing or remanding.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: State UI law higher-authority appeal and Social Security Act s. 303(a)(3) fair hearing

evidence.note: Higher-authority timing varies widely by state; estimate.

exceptions.name: Identity flag
exceptions.description: Automated checks cannot confirm identity, so the claimant must submit documents, often calls the contact center, and an examiner reviews them; in 2020 and 2021 fraud attacks made this far more common.

exceptions.name: Monetarily ineligible or wage dispute
exceptions.description: Base-period wages are too low; some claimants supply missing wages and are redetermined eligible.

exceptions.name: Separation adjudication
exceptions.description: The claimant quit or was discharged, or the employer contests, so an adjudicator holds fact-finding before any payment.

exceptions.name: Nonseparation issue before first payment
exceptions.description: An availability, job refusal, school or income question on the first certifications is adjudicated before payment.

exceptions.name: Claimant appeal
exceptions.description: A denied claimant appeals and a hearing officer holds a telephone hearing; about a third of decisions reverse the denial.

exceptions.name: Employer appeal of an allowed claim
exceptions.description: The employer appeals an allowance after benefits have started; payments continue while the appeal is heard.

exceptions.name: Higher-authority appeal
exceptions.description: The losing party appeals the hearing decision to the board of review.

exceptions.name: Claim surge backlog
exceptions.description: In 2020 and 2021, claim volume rose several-fold, so identity, adjudication and appeal queues grew from days to months; this is shown in the benchmarks rather than in the step times.

pain_points.description: During the 2020 to 2022 surge first payments slowed sharply: the share within 14 days fell from 82% in 2019 to 58% to 64%.
Appeal backlogs: the share of first-level decisions within 30 days fell from 72% in 2019 to 11% in 2021 and 16% in 2022, far below the 60% federal criterion.

Separation adjudication depends on reaching both parties by phone; employers often respond late or not at all, and determinations miss the 21-day target about a third of the time even in normal years.

evidence.note: 65.8% within 21 days in 2019.

pain_points.description: Identity verification holds and document reviews stall legitimate claims and drive contact center calls, while fraud attempts surged in 2020 and 2021.

evidence.note: Widely reported during the period; no rate was sourced.

pain_points.description: Monetary ineligibility more than doubled during the surge (10% in 2019, 23% to 44% in 2020 to 2022), adding wage disputes and redeterminations.

assumptions: Step times and branch shares are set for normal operations, calibrated to 2019 national ETA reports; 2020 to 2022 surge conditions appear only in the benchmarks and pain points.

Most states have a one-week unpaid waiting week, so the first compensable week ends about 13 days after filing; non-waiting-week states pay about a week sooner. The certification wait (5 to 16 days) blends both.

Sequential model: issue detection really happens at filing or when the employer responds, during the certification wait; the adjudication queue is shortened so that detection to determination matches the 2019 ETA 9052 median band.
The 33% separation issue rate sits between 0.26 (per total initial claim) and 0.40 (per new claim) separation determinations in 2019 ETA 207 data.
Shares for identity flags (10%), nonseparation issues before first payment (8%), appeal after denial (35% separation, 20% nonseparation) and board appeals (7%) are estimates.
Claimant and employer time is outside the agency and is shown as waiting with zero hands-on time; contact center work counts only identity-related calls on initial claims.
Hands-on times per step and the resulting staffing (about one staff hour per initial claim across identity, adjudication and appeals) are estimates; no minutes-per-unit figures were sourced.
The process ends at the first payment for paid claims; continued weekly claims, later nonmonetary issues and overpayment recovery are out of scope.
An employer appeal reversed in the employer's favor would create an overpayment; the model routes all favorable-to-appellant decisions to payment, which slightly overstates paid outcomes.
Loaded costs use BLS May 2021 wages times about 1.9 (benefits factor 1.62 from BLS ECEC for state and local government plus about 20% overhead).
The web search budget ran out during research, so identity verification guidance (UIPL) and state law details could not be opened and those controls rest on general knowledge.
